quick.summary: Why a pipeline that never fails can be the most dangerous one.
quick.takeaway: Catch only what you can handle. Let the rest fail loudly.

beats.line: My job ran green all month. The table has been empty for a week. How?
Does your code catch every error and carry on?
Yes. I did not want it to crash.
Then it hid the failure. That is called swallowing the error.
Catch only errors you can handle, like a timeout.
Let everything else stop the job, loudly.
And log which file and row it was on.
A failed job at night wakes someone up, though.
Better one alert tonight than a week of missing data.
Try a timeout again twice. Anything else fails and names the file.
Now a green run means the data really arrived.

quiz.question: A pipeline step hits an unexpected error. What should the code do?
options: Stop the job and log what it was processing
Write an empty table and finish
quiz.explanation: Failing loudly with context shows the problem at once; hiding it produces missing data nobody notices.

quiz.question: Code that catches every error and continues makes a pipeline more reliable.
quiz.explanation: It hides failures. The job looks healthy while the data is missing or wrong.
